what: Burlington Stores is an off-price retailer. It buys branded clothing, home goods and accessories opportunistically and sells them below department store prices, with stock that changes constantly.
customers: Value-seeking American shoppers across income levels, including middle-income customers trading down.
money: branded clothing for the whole family
home goods, beauty products and toys
moat: Buying power and flexible store layouts that let it take whatever branded inventory becomes available, a model that needs scale and supplier relationships built over decades.
risks: Operating margin of 7% is below its larger off-price rivals
Debt of about $5.9 billion including leases
Tariffs raise the cost of imported merchandise
opportunities: Revenue grew about 9% last year and about 10% a year over three years
Analysts see about 40% upside from current levels
Department store closures free up branded inventory and shoppers for off-price retailers
watch: Comparable store sales and the gap in operating margin against TJX and Ross.
